experiment: E13 deep-history graph layout, only the observed worktree state before publication
decision: on a 300,000-commit repository the layout a graph capture waits for fell from 377.7 to 408.4 ms, both worktree states, to 153.0 to 172.5 ms, the observed state only; the other state is laid out after publication in the background (68c7e75d)
scope: backend only, timed in-process around trunk_git::graph::capture_remembering and GraphSnapshot construction in a release build; not the app's open or commit-to-usable time, not the frontend, not whether the background layout finishes before the user's next edit; one machine, three alternating runs per build
comparativeVerdict: after faster in every reading, ranges disjoint (before min 377.7 ms, after max 172.5 ms)
machine: Apple M5 Pro, 48 GB, macOS, release profile with debug = 1, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 for the build only; load average about 3 during the runs

builds.before: trunk-git exported with git archive at 68c7e75d^
builds.after: trunk-git exported with git archive at 68c7e75d

fixture.build: git init <dir>; python3 generator.py 300000 | git -C <dir> fast-import --quiet
fixture.storage: one pack written by fast-import, no commit-graph file
fixture.reuse: the probe adds no commits, so one copy served every run

procedure: per run: open the repository, time one capture with a fresh CommitMemo (open.captureMs) and GraphSnapshot::new (open.layoutMs); then seven times: open a fresh handle, time a capture with the memo held (captureMs), GraphSnapshot::new (layoutMs), and with_worktree_dirty of the other state (firstOtherStateMs), which in the after build is the layout the background task takes off the first edit, since the probe never runs it. Runs alternate before, after, three times.
generator:
import sys, random
random.seed(7)
n = int(sys.argv[1])
out = sys.stdout.buffer
t = 1_600_000_000
marks = {}
mark = 0
heads = {"main": None, "feature": None, "topic": None}
def commit(branch, parents, ts):
    global mark
    mark += 1
    msg = f"commit {mark} on {branch}\n".encode()
    out.write(f"commit refs/heads/{branch}\nmark :{mark}\n".encode())
    out.write(f"author A <a@x> {ts} +0000\ncommitter A <a@x> {ts} +0000\n".encode())
    out.write(f"data {len(msg)}\n".encode() + msg)
    if parents:
        out.write(f"from :{parents[0]}\n".encode())
        for p in parents[1:]:
            out.write(f"merge :{p}\n".encode())
    out.write(f"M 644 inline f{mark % 50}.txt\ndata 2\n{mark % 10}\n".encode())
    out.write(b"\n")
    return mark
for i in range(n):
    # same-second runs, like scripted or rebased commits
    if random.random() < 0.7: t += random.randint(1, 600)
    r = random.random()
    if heads["main"] and r < 0.04 and heads["feature"]:
        m = commit("main", [heads["main"], heads["feature"]], t); heads["main"] = m
    elif r < 0.25 and heads["main"]:
        b = "feature" if r < 0.15 else "topic"
        base = heads[b] or heads["main"]
        heads[b] = commit(b, [base], t)
    else:
        heads["main"] = commit("main", [heads["main"]] if heads["main"] else [], t)
limitations: the probe never starts the background layout, so firstOtherStateMs is the cost of the first edit when the background task has not run; whether it finishes before a real first edit was not timed in the app
the commit message of 68c7e75d quotes 506 to 541 ms before and 172 to 235 ms after from earlier single, unalternated probe runs; these alternating runs are the record
cold capture, about 1.09 s here, is unchanged; git rev-list --topo-order --all took 0.95 to 1.1 s on the same fixture in an earlier reading
